title: Have a Heart and Lost in Meditation: titles change
summary: Have a Heart is the original title of Lost in Meditation; publishers or Duke changed titles to fit lyrics.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There is a number from 1938 called 'Have a Heart'. Have a Heart?

It must be Mills, because the composer credits -- one place they say Tizol and Ellington and the other one -- no, I beg your pardon. No. They say Tizol, Ellington, Singer and Mills. So if it's got Mills' name on it, it must've been published by Mills, right? I think that one I got from -- oh, I beg your pardon. 'Have a Heart' is the other title for Lost in Meditation.' That's been recorded under two titles, I guess. Do you remember that?
Well, maybe that's what they decided to call it, and then they changed it and just left it Lost in Meditation, you know?
But you don't remember the name, Have a Heart?
Okay. I guess that must have been the original one.

Let me tell you -- there are a lot of things that I wrote where I put a title on maybe for the time being, but the publishers would always change it, or either Duke Ellington or the publishers would change it according to the lyrics, you know?
